title: Valid Parentheses
description: Given a string `s` made only of the characters `(`, `)`, `{`, `}`, `[` and `]`, return `true` if it is valid. A string is valid when every opening bracket is closed by the same type of bracket and brackets close in the correct order (each closer matches the most recent unclosed opener).

examples.explanation: The ] arrives while ( is the most recent open bracket.

hints: The most recently opened bracket must be the first one closed. Which structure gives last-in, first-out?
Push each opener. On a closer, compare it with what is on top of that structure.
If a closer arrives when the stack is empty or the top does not match, return false. At the end the stack must be empty.

solution.explanation: Use a stack. Push every opening bracket. For a closing bracket, the stack must be non-empty and its top must be the matching opener, which is then popped; otherwise the string is invalid. After the scan the stack must be empty or some opener was never closed. One pass: O(n) time and O(n) space.
